name: Dodge City & the Flint Hills
summary: The rowdiest cattle town of the Old West, and the last great swath of tallgrass prairie in America.

lodging.name: A Dodge City hotel, then the Flint Hills

foodMustTry.name: A Kansas beef steak
foodMustTry.blurb: In the heart of cattle country.

item.title: Boot Hill Museum & Front Street

location.name: Boot Hill Museum
location.address: 500 W Wyatt Earp Blvd, Dodge City, KS

item.blurb: The reconstructed Front Street, the Long Branch Saloon, and the cattle-town legend of Wyatt Earp and 'Gunsmoke.'

item.title: Tallgrass Prairie National Preserve
item.blurb: Drive east into the rolling Flint Hills to walk the last major stand of tallgrass prairie, with its bison herd.

rest.label: The prairie, unhurried
rest.note: There is nothing here, which is the entire point and the hardest thing on this itinerary to put on a clock. Walk out into the tallgrass until you can't hear the road any more, and stay a while. This is the last of the original prairie — ninety-six percent of it is gone.
